briefing.opening: Good morning, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for October 25, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Increasing Climate Threats and Warnings
sections.content: The direct impacts of climate change are becoming increasingly clear and severe worldwide. According to reports, rising sea levels and land subsidence, both caused by climate change, are occurring simultaneously, leading to parts of the global landmass disappearing underwater [5]. Internationally, news that summer storms intensified by climate change are exacerbating mold problems in Chicago-area schools highlights a direct threat to living environments [45]. Furthermore, a report indicating that Portugal's chestnut production is being affected by climate change suggests widespread impacts on ecosystems and local economies [50]. These series of reports once again remind us that climate change is a complex and difficult challenge, likened to a 'terrible Gordian knot' [48].

sections.title: 🌱 Expansion of Domestic Carbon Neutrality Practices and Local Community Efforts
sections.content: Domestically, various local community-level efforts are actively underway to achieve carbon neutrality. Seongdong-gu has initiated specific adaptation research by creating a 'research garden' to respond to climate change and conducting growth experiments with 225 plant species [1, 3]. Gangnam-gu successfully concluded a performance-sharing session for carbon neutrality education tailored to young children, with 15 private kindergartens participating, thereby contributing to fostering environmental awareness in future generations [6, 10, 13, 14, 17, 19]. Gwangmyeong-si is promoting the value of carbon neutrality to its citizens and encouraging its practice through upcycling waste resources and donation activities [9, 18], and is expanding everyday participation through initiatives such as operating 'visiting apartment carbon neutrality experience booths' [15] and Suseong-gu, Daegu's commitment to carbon neutrality practices [12]. The Suwon Youth Foundation signed a business agreement with the Suwon Climate Change Experience Education Center to create an eco-friendly local community with youth and young adults [4].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 The Reality and Challenges of Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is showing continuous progress but faces realistic policy and infrastructural challenges. Domestically, despite renewable energy facility capacity surpassing that of coal, actual power generation from coal is three times higher than from renewables, indicating the need for efficiency improvements [26]. While the Ministry of Climate is introducing a renewable energy target management system for public institutions in line with the abolition of RPS (Renewable Portfolio Standard) and is considering expanding it to local public enterprises [25, 37], the cost of RECs (Renewable Energy Certificates) for long-term renewable energy contracts reaching approximately 90 trillion KRW and the freezing of climate and environmental charges since 2023 demonstrate the economic burden [35]. Furthermore, despite increasing solar and nuclear power generation, the slow progress in completing power grids to transmit electricity is causing difficulties in power transmission [40], and Tokyo Gas's abandonment of the Fukushima offshore wind power project [24] illustrates the challenges faced by large-scale renewable energy projects. Assemblyman Lee Heon-seung argued that the expansion of renewable energy is suppressing the reflection of climate and environment-related electricity charges [28], and the complex alliances, likened to 'o-wol-dong-ju' (sharing a boat in rough waters), formed by entities related to coal, LNG, and renewable energy [22] necessitate a cautious approach to energy transition policies.

sections.title: 🌱 Trends in Eco-Friendly Technology Innovation and Infrastructure Development
sections.content: Efforts for eco-friendly technology innovation and infrastructure development to address climate change are actively being pursued both domestically and internationally. WIPO (World Intellectual Property Organization) is actively promoting technology commercialization and financial linkages beyond green patent development, seeking practical solutions to the climate crisis [2]. Domestically, the Carbon Neutrality and Clean Energy Industry Promotion Association has been launched [11], and industrial technological contributions continue, such as Hyundai Air Conditioning proposing carbon neutrality solutions with its turbo chiller and heat source optimal control technology [7]. In Yeongdeok-gun, numerous renewable energy projects, including a 631.6 MW wind power project, are being promoted [23], and local community efforts to build renewable energy infrastructure are becoming visible, with Hamyang residents appealing for a signature campaign to designate an 8 GW complex renewable energy special zone [32, 33]. Furthermore, Hoseo University is expanding its ESG management and fostering talent in carbon neutrality and green finance [8, 16], and at the recent Paris Motor Show, ultra-compact electric vehicles that can contribute to alleviating urban parking problems and reducing carbon emissions garnered attention [41, 42].

sections.title: 🌍 International Climate Action and Responsibility Discussions
sections.content: The international community is strengthening its actions to address climate change, with discussions intensifying particularly on the costs and responsibilities of damages. Nepal's receipt of 21.6 million dollars as the first climate crisis compensation is regarded as a significant advancement in the Loss and Damage compensation mechanism for climate change [43]. Meanwhile, the question of whether taxpayers or fossil fuel companies should bear the costs of climate change damages is heading to the Supreme Court, intensifying legal and social discussions on accountability [44]. Various response efforts from civil societies and governments worldwide continue, such as Georgetown University student groups independently leading climate action [46] and Lithuania launching a climate change map [49]. However, international climate policies still face complex interests and debates, as exemplified by cases revealing environmental differences of opinion surrounding climate change and fracking [47].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the active carbon neutrality efforts and the reality of renewable energy transition unfolding both domestically and internationally, even amidst increasing climate threats, as well as discussions on international responsibility. Continued attention and cooperation will be key to overcoming the climate crisis. This concludes today's climate briefing.
